Tomato___Early_blight.description: Early blight is a fungal disease (Alternaria solani) causing dark concentric-ring spots on older leaves, which eventually yellow and drop.
prevention_steps: Remove and destroy infected leaves promptly.
Avoid overhead watering; water at the base of the plant.
Apply a copper-based or chlorothalonil fungicide as needed.
Rotate crops and avoid planting tomatoes in the same spot each year.

Tomato___Late_blight.description: Late blight (Phytophthora infestans) causes large, water-soaked, grey-green lesions on leaves and stems that spread rapidly in cool, wet weather.
prevention_steps: Destroy infected plants immediately to stop spread.
Improve air circulation and avoid overhead irrigation.
Apply a preventive fungicide during humid periods.
Use resistant tomato varieties where available.

Tomato___healthy.description: This leaf shows no visible signs of disease and appears healthy.
prevention_steps: Continue regular watering and balanced fertilization.
Monitor leaves weekly for early signs of pests or disease.
Maintain good airflow between plants.

Potato___Early_blight.description: Early blight in potatoes causes dark brown spots with concentric rings, typically starting on older, lower leaves.
prevention_steps: Remove infected foliage and dispose of it away from the field.
Use certified disease-free seed potatoes.
Apply fungicide at the first sign of symptoms.
Practice 2-3 year crop rotation.

Potato___Late_blight.description: Late blight is a fast-spreading fungal-like disease causing dark, water-soaked lesions on leaves and stems, often with a white mold ring on the underside.
prevention_steps: Destroy infected plants to prevent spread to healthy ones.
Avoid overhead watering and reduce leaf wetness duration.
Apply fungicide proactively in cool, wet conditions.
Plant resistant potato varieties.

Apple___Apple_scab.description: Apple scab is caused by the fungus Venturia inaequalis, producing olive-green to black velvety spots on leaves and fruit.
prevention_steps: Rake and destroy fallen leaves each autumn to reduce spores.
Apply fungicide sprays starting at bud break.
Prune trees to improve air circulation.
Choose scab-resistant apple varieties for new plantings.

Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.description: Common rust appears as small, reddish-brown pustules scattered across both leaf surfaces, caused by the fungus Puccinia sorghi.
prevention_steps: Plant rust-resistant corn hybrids.
Avoid excessive nitrogen fertilization.
Apply foliar fungicide if infection is severe before tasseling.
Monitor fields regularly during warm, humid weather.
